title: Operational Eval & Rollout Playbook for Mixed-Precision Deployments
author: Lena Ortega
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes how to evaluate, certify, and safely roll out mixed-precision model variants (FP16/INT8/Hybrid) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. It ties together eval-harness integration, prompt/benchmark selection, runtime guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage triggers so teams can operationalize mixed-precision as a first-class cost/performance lever.

Goals:
- Deliver an end-to-end checklist for certifying a quantized/mixed-precision candidate for production serving.
- Define objective eval signals, SLOs, and rollback criteria that map to production reliability and user-facing quality.
- Provide concrete tooling/commands and integration points with the eval harness and monitoring pipelines.

Audience:
- ML Engineers onboarding model variants into the inference fleet.
- Applied ML and SRE owners running rollouts and on-call.
- Product owners who must sign off on quality trade-offs.

Context and scope:
- Applies to: model families served by Redwood (causal LLMs and encoder-decoder where supported).
- Not covered: full model training; this focuses solely on inference-time quantization and mixed-precision execution paths.

High-level strategy:
1) Pre-eval: baseline capture and workload fingerprinting.
2) Offline evals: fidelity, prompt coverage, and edgecase stress tests in the eval harness.
3) Shadow validation: telemetry-aligned shadowing against production traffic.
4) Canary rollout: small-ratio low-latency canary with active monitoring for regressions.
5) Fast rollback / fallback: automated fallback to FP16/present variant on signal.

1) Pre-eval: baseline capture and fingerprinting
- Owner: model-onboarding team + applied-ml.
- Steps:
  1. Capture baseline metrics for the current production variant (tokens/sec, p95 latency, cost per 1M tokens, response-accuracy on golden prompt set). Use prod-metrics export: service=redwood-serving, metric=token_latency_histogram, tag=model:<prod-model>, date_range=last_7d.
  2. Fingerprint workload slices: short-prompts (<64 tokens), long-context (>1024 tokens), multi-turn chats, tool-calls, and embedding-like requests. Store fingerprint id in the model registry.
  3. Select canonical prompt subsets for evaluation: a) high-frequency prompts (top 200 by count), b) failure-prone prompts (annotated), c) coverage slices (synthetic adversarial probes).

2) Offline evals (eval-harness integration)
- Owner: eval-harness + applied-ml.
- Required artifacts:
  - Quantization profile metadata (.qprof) describing per-layer scale factors and fallback paths.
  - Eval manifest JSON listing prompt IDs and expected metrics (format compatible with evaluator-sdk).
  - Diff-seed set for deterministic sampling (seed ranges: 0..999).
- Minimum tests to pass (all run in eval-harness):
  a) Fidelity suite: token-level BLEU/ROUGE-style proxies + semantic similarity (embedding cosine > 0.92 on canonical prompts).
  b) Stability suite: repeated-seed generation variance check (response variance < 6% normalized score).
  c) Safety guardrail suite: no increase in flagged safety categories above 0.5% absolute over baseline.
  d) Latency/cost simulation: model-internal latency profile under standard batching (batch sizes 1, 4, 16) and KV cache hit/miss scenarios.
- Pass criteria (default):
  - Semantic similarity >= 0.92 AND per-slice degradation <= 2% for short/medium prompts.
  - For long-context slices (>1024): relative output drift <= 3.5%.
  - No safety category regression beyond threshold.
- Commands (example):
  - Run local harness (Docker): docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data redwood/eval-harness:stable "--manifest /data/my_eval_manifest.json --model-variant mymodel-int8.qprof --seed 42 --out /data/results.json"

3) Shadow validation (telemetry-aligned)
- Owner: applied-ml + eng-sre.
- Objective: Validate behavior on live-like traffic without affecting users.
- Steps:
  1. Configure shadow route: route policy = shadow-to:<mymodel-mixed-precision>, sampling = 5% of requests from production routing table R001.
  2. Collect paired responses for 48–72 hours and compute: token-wise divergence, end-to-end latency delta, and cost delta.
  3. Annotate 500 randomly sampled mismatches for human review (priority to failures hitting business-critical intents).
- Shadow pass thresholds:
  - End-to-end latency p95 increase < 12ms on Dedicated; < 25ms on Hosted.
  - Token divergence rate < 1.5% absolute on high-frequency prompts.
  - No new API error classes introduced.

4) Canary rollout (gradual traffic ramp)
- Owner: eng-platform + oncall.
- Canary plan (example):
  1. Canary-0: 0.5% traffic, 1 hour. Verify health metrics and error budget consumption.
  2. Canary-1: 2% traffic, 6 hours. Run automated snapshot tests against the eval-harness backlog every 30 minutes.
  3. Canary-2: 10% traffic, 24 hours. Activate human review pipeline and SLO alarms.
  4. Ramp to 30% for 24 hours if no alerts, then consider full rollout or dedicated capacity rollout.
- Automated checks during canary (must be green to progress):
  - Quality signals: semantic similarity on rolling window >= pass threshold, response-stability index within variance budget.
  - Reliability signals: 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.05%, queue-length SLOs not breached.
  - Cost signals: per-token cost reduction >= 12% or neutral (depending on business goal).
- Failure handling: immediate rollback to previous variant if any of the following occurs:
  - Safety regression spike > 0.25% absolute (30-min window).
  - Latency p95 regression > configured SLO (default: +25ms hosted, +10ms dedicated).
  - Increase in customer-impacting errors (authentication/authorization/response-corruption) above 0.1% absolute.

5) Fast rollback and fallback policies
- Owner: eng-platform + serving-runtime.
- Mechanisms:
  - Automated variant fallback: runtime policy configured to route requests to primary FP16 variant when model returns non-conforming outputs or explicit error codes (ERROR_CODE_QUANT_EXEC).
  - On-call playbook: see related runbook id: PR-ONCALL-quant-fallback (link internal).
  - Postmortem telemetry preserved for triage (pair traces, shard ids, kernels used).

Quality guardrails and monitoring mapping
- Key metrics to monitor (service=redwood-serving):
  - production.semantic_similarity.rolling_30m (threshold: >= 0.92),
  - production.token_divergence_rate.rolling_30m (threshold: <= 0.015),
  - production.latency.p95 (baseline + tolerance),
  - production.safety_flag_rate.rolling_30m (absolute thresholds in safety SLO doc),
  - production.error_ratio.rolling_5m (critical threshold: baseline + 0.001).
- Alerting policies (examples):
  - P1: safety_flag_rate > baseline + 0.25% for 15m -> page oncall and initiate rollback.
  - P2: semantic_similarity < pass threshold for 3 consecutive 30m windows -> notify applied-ml and pause rollout.

Regression triage hooks (what to collect on signal)
- Required artifacts captured automatically on any canary or shadow regression alert:
  - paired request/response payloads (redacted for PII), generation seeds, model variant id, kernel/precision trace, and hardware affinity.
  - evaluator-harness replay job spec that reproduces the failure with the same seed.
  - human annotation batch id assigned to the top-100 mismatches.
- Triage owner: regression-triage team + model owner. Expected TTR (time-to-resolution): 72 hours for critical regressions.

Quantization profile governance
- Profile naming convention: <model>-<arch>-<precision>-v<semver> (e.g., gptx-arch1-int8-v1).
- Required metadata fields in profile: created_by, create_date, calibration_dataset_id, fallback_policy, supported_kernels, expected_accuracy_delta_pct, intended_deployment_tiers (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Sign-off: applied-ml lead + product PM must sign off for any profile that alters output semantics > 1%.

Operational checklist (short)
1. Create quant profile and run local eval-harness fidelity + stability tests.
2. Record baseline metrics and fingerprint workload.
3. Run shadow test for 48–72 hours with paired telemetry.
4. Execute canary plan with automated checks.
5. Escalate immediately on P1 signals and trigger rollback.

Appendix A: Example evaluators and CLI snippets
- Generate evaluator manifest template (YAML snippet):
  ---
  manifest_version: 1
  model_variant: gptx-arch1-int8-v1
  prompts: /eval/canonical_prompts/top200.json
  slices: [short, long, tool_call, safety]
  seeds: [42, 99, 101]

- Example monitor query (Datadog):
  - query: avg:last_5m:production.semantic_similarity{model_variant:gptx-arch1-int8-v1}.rollup(avg)

Notes and rationale:
- Thresholds chosen to bias conservative rollouts for Hosted customers where latency variation is more visible. Dedicated customers may tighten latency tolerances and accept larger per-token cost for stability.
- Mixed-precision is codified as a cost control: teams should capture unit economics (cost per 1M tokens) pre/post and ensure no more than 5% net loss in user-facing quality unless explicitly approved by product.
